paper.title: Sublinear Optimal Policy Value Estimation in Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Disjoint linear contextual bandit, OPT estimation, known covariance setting (passive sampling)
unmapped: Disjoint linear reward model: y_{a,j} = beta_a^T x_j + b_a + eta, a separate unknown d-dim parameter per arm
Contexts drawn i.i.d. from N(0, Sigma) with Sigma known
Objective is estimating the optimal policy value OPT = E_x[max_a (beta_a^T x + b_a)] to additive error eps, without returning a policy
Noise only has bounded variance E[eta^2] <= sigma^2; reward variances sigma_a bounded by a constant
Passive data collection: N i.i.d. samples per arm
settings.definition_quote: the reward $y$ from pulling an arm $a$ in a context $\x_j$ is $y_{a,j}=\beta_a^T\x_j+b_a+\eta_{a,j}$. ... $\E[\eta]=0, \E[\eta^2]\le \sigma^2$ ... our goal is to predict the expected reward of the optimal policy ... $OPT:= \E_{\x}[\max_a(\beta_a^T\x+b_a)]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Disjoint linear contextual bandit, OPT estimation, unknown covariance setting
unmapped: Disjoint linear reward model with a separate d-dim parameter per arm
Contexts drawn i.i.d. from N(0, Sigma) with Sigma unknown, sigma_min I <= Sigma <= sigma_max I
The learner knows sigma_min and sigma_max (spectral bounds of the context covariance)
Objective is estimating the optimal policy value OPT to additive error eps
Passive data collection: N i.i.d. samples per arm
settings.definition_quote: we prove an analog of Corollary~\ref{cor:isotropic} in the setting where the contexts $\x$ are drawn from a Gaussian distribution with arbitrary \emph{unknown} covariance.

settings.name_in_paper: Unknown covariance with a large set of unlabeled examples
unmapped: Disjoint linear reward model with a separate d-dim parameter per arm
Contexts i.i.d. N(0, Sigma), Sigma unknown, plus access to an additional set of unlabeled contexts
Objective is estimating the optimal policy value OPT to additive error eps
settings.definition_quote: we present one extreme case where there is a sufficiently large set of unlabeled examples (size $\Omega(d)$), and the problem essentially becomes a known covariance problem.

unmapped: Disjoint linear reward model with a separate d-dim parameter per arm
Contexts i.i.d. from a known mixture of M Gaussians with bounded component means and covariances
Objective is estimating the optimal policy value OPT to additive error eps
settings.definition_quote: Suppose each context $\x$ is drawn independently from a mixture of Gaussian distribution $\sum_{i=1}^M \alpha_i N(\mu_i,\Sigma_i)$, and the parameters $\mu_i, \Sigma_i, \alpha_i$ are all known to the algorithm.

unmapped: Disjoint linear reward model with a separate d-dim parameter per arm
Contexts i.i.d. N(0, I_d), known covariance
Objective is estimating the optimal policy value OPT to additive error eps
settings.definition_quote: Assuming we are in the contextual mult-armed bandit setting where each context $\x_i$ is drawn from $N(0,I_d)$, and a bandit is defined by the set of $K$ coefficient vectors $(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_K)$.

algorithms.name: Algorithm 1 (Main Algorithm for Estimating OPT) with Algorithm 2 (known covariance) / Algorithm 3 (unknown covariance)

conditions: contexts i.i.d. N(0, Sigma) with known Sigma
reward standard deviations sigma_a bounded by a constant
epsilon >= sqrt(log K)/d^(1/4)
tuning: n = Theta(sqrt(d) log K / eps^2) samples per arm per repetition, ceil(48(log(K^2/delta)+1)) repetitions

source.label: cor:isotropic
source.quote: In the known covariance setting, for any $\eps\ge \frac{\sqrt{\log K}}{d^{1/4}}$, with probability $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:main} estimates the optimal reward $OPT$ with additive error $\eps$ using a total number of samples $T = \Theta(\frac{\sqrt{d}K\log K}{\eps^2} \log (K/\delta)).$

results.notes: Sample complexity to estimate OPT within additive error eps w.p. 1-delta; passive uniform sampling over arms.

symbols.n_rep: number of samples per arm in each of the Theta(log(K/delta)) repetitions (total per arm N = Theta(n log(K/delta)))

conditions: contexts i.i.d. N(0, Sigma) with known Sigma
reward standard deviations sigma_a bounded by a constant

source.label: thm:iso
source.quote: In the known covariance setting, with probability at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:main} estimates the expected reward of the optimal policy with error bounded as follows: $|OPT-\widehat{OPT}| = O(\sqrt{\log K}(\frac{d+n}{n^2})^{1/4})$

results.notes: Bound on estimation error of OPT (not regret). Proof gives explicit constant 10*sqrt(log K)((3d+n)/n^2)^{1/4} * sigma_bar.

symbols.k: degree parameter of the polynomial approximation (any positive integer)
symbols.s_unl: number of unlabeled examples (s = Kn/2 after sample splitting)
symbols.sigma_min: minimum eigenvalue of context covariance Sigma
symbols.sigma_max: maximum eigenvalue of context covariance Sigma

conditions: contexts i.i.d. N(0, Sigma), Sigma unknown with sigma_min I <= Sigma <= sigma_max I
reward standard deviations bounded by a constant
tuning: polynomial of degree k+2 approximating f(x)=x on [sigma_min, sigma_max]

source.label: thm:unknownc
source.quote: In the unknown covariance setting, for any positive integer $k$, with probability $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:main} estimates the optimal reward OPT with additive error: ... where $f(k) = k^{O(k)}$.

results.notes: Estimation error of OPT; f(k)=k^{O(k)} recorded as symbol.

symbols.k: min(C_1 sqrt(log K)/eps + 2, sqrt(sigma_max/sigma_min)(log(log K/eps^2) + C_2))

conditions: contexts i.i.d. N(0, Sigma), Sigma unknown with sigma_min I <= Sigma <= sigma_max I
epsilon > sqrt(log K)/d^(1/4)
tuning: k = min(C_1 sqrt(log K)/eps + 2, sqrt(sigma_max/sigma_min)(log(log K/eps^2)+C_2))

source.label: cor:unknown
source.quote: For any $\eps>\frac{\sqrt{\log K}}{d^{1/4}}$, with probability $1-\delta$, Algorithm 1 estimates the optimal reward OPT with additive error $\eps$ using a total number of $T = \Theta\Big(\log(K/\delta)\max(k^{O(1)}d^{1-1/k}K^{2/k}, \frac{k^{O(k)}K \log K\sqrt{d}}{\eps^2})\Big)$ samples, where $k = \min(C_1\sqrt{\log K}/\eps+2, ...)$

results.notes: k^{O(1)} and k^{O(k)} factors recorded as symbols g_k and f_k.

conditions: sigma_min I <= Sigma <= sigma_max I with sigma_max/sigma_min a constant
epsilon constant
delta constant

source.label: cor:main-gen
source.quote: Assuming that the covariance of the context $\x_i$ satisfies $\sigma_{\min} I_d \preceq \Sigma\preceq \sigma_{\max} I$ and $\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}$ is a constant, for constant $\eps$, Algorithm 1 takes $\sigma_{\min}, \sigma_{\max}$, and a total number of $T = O(d^{1-\frac{C}{\log\log K+\log(1/\eps)}}K^{\gamma}+\sqrt{d}K^{1+\gamma})$ samples

results.notes: Special case of Corollary 7; the statement does not explicitly say 'estimates OPT to error eps' but this is implied by context.

conditions: contexts i.i.d. N(0, Sigma), Sigma unknown
access to an additional set of unlabeled examples of size Theta((d + log(1/delta)) log^2 K / eps^4)
tuning: covariance estimated from unlabeled examples; contexts whitened by hat Sigma^{-1/2} and known-covariance Algorithm 1 run

source.label: cor:gen-unlabeled
source.quote: In the unknown covariance setting, there is an algorithm that estimates the optimal reward OPT with additive error $\eps$ with probability $1-\delta$ using a total number of labeled examples $T = \Theta(\frac{\sqrt{d}K\log K}{\eps^2} \log (K/\delta)),$ and a set of unlabeled examples of size $\Theta((d+\log 1/\delta)\log^2 K/\eps^4)$

results.notes: T counts labeled examples only; unlabeled sample count is in conditions.

conditions: contexts from a known mixture of M Gaussians
||mu_i|| and ||Sigma_i|| bounded by a constant
epsilon >= sqrt(log K)/d^(1/4)

source.label: thm:main-mog
source.quote: Suppose each context $\x$ is drawn independently from a mixture of Gaussian distribution ... Then for any $\eps\ge \frac{\sqrt{\log K}}{d^{1/4}}$, with probability $1-\delta$, there is an algorithm that estimate the optimal reward $OPT$ with additive error $\eps$ using a total number of samples $T = \Theta(\frac{\sqrt{d}K\log K}{\eps^2}\log (KM/\delta)).$

results.notes: Algorithm is a per-component variant of Algorithm 1.

conditions: passive algorithms: N i.i.d. samples per arm (uniform sampling)
success probability greater than 2/3
contexts N(0, I), Gaussian noise

source.label: thm:lb
source.quote: There exists a constant $C$ such that for any $\eps>0$ given $T = C\frac{\sqrt{d}K\log K}{\eps^2}$ samples (equivalently $N = C\frac{\sqrt{d}\log K}{\eps^2}$ samples for each arm), no algorithm can estimate the optimal reward with expected additive error less than $\eps$ with probability greater than $2/3$.

results.notes: Passive setting lower bound; matches Corollary 1 up to log(K/delta).

conditions: fully adaptive algorithms allowed
success probability at least 2/3
contexts N(0, I_d), Gaussian noise

source.label: thm:lb-adaptive
source.quote: There exists a constant $C$ such that no algorithm can estimate the optimal reward with additive error $\eps$ and probability of success at least $2/3$ using a number of rounds that is less than $T = C\frac{\sqrt{d}K}{\eps^{2}\log^{3/2}(dK)}.$

results.notes: Holds for adaptive algorithms choosing which arm to play on each context.
